question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Cut to the chase
solution:
The correct answer is **"To get to the point."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Cut to the chase"** is an idiom that means to get to the point without wasting time. (बिना समय बर्बाद किये मुद्दे पर आना)

 
 
• **Example**:* I didn't have long to talk, so I **cut to the chase**__ and asked whether he was still married.*
 
 
 
• This phrase is often used in situations where someone is giving a long explanation or story, and the listener wants them to skip to the important part.
 
• The origin of this phrase is uncertain, but it may come from early Hollywood films where chase scenes were a common feature.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.
